Documentation photograph of a contemporary art installation: A single monumental lightbox stands alone in a vast, dark, empty exhibition hall; one visitor has stopped in front of it.

References: Image 1 is THE LIGHTBOX: our tall freestanding gallery lightbox; take its exact slim matte black frame, depth, low steel feet and evenly lit opal face, scaled as the shot says. The output is one single photograph, portrait 4:5.

Composition A, centred and symmetric: the design surface sits on the centre line, square to the camera, with even space on both sides; strong verticals and horizontals run parallel to the frame. Shot: Camera at chest height straight on, 35mm lens, f/4. The lightbox, scaled up to about four metres tall, stands on the centre line and fills about 65 percent of the frame height; its glow spills across a polished grey concrete floor and makes a long soft reflection of it below; a low ceiling with one long recessed light slot runs across the top edge; dark walls fall away to black at both sides; one visitor stands far to the right of it. Visitors appear only as small dark silhouettes, seen from behind against the light, never more than a fraction of the frame; no face or profile shows.

Place: A real art space or real outdoor site exactly as the shot describes, quiet and spare; the installation is the only thing that glows.

Light: The installation's own glow is the main light: it spills onto the floor, walls and people around it and falls off into deep shadow. Any other light is the real ambient light named in the shot.

Palette and grade: Neutral and cool: charcoal, concrete grey, soft blacks and natural skin; the glowing design surface is pure neutral white; no teal, green or orange cast, except the natural blue of snow at blue hour where the shot names it.

Real: this is a product mockup photograph of an art installation, so the design surface is the hero: it is large in the frame and the camera is close enough that it dominates, the way an exhibition photographer frames the work, never a tiny object in a big room. It is a real photograph made in camera by an art documentation photographer, not a render. The design surface faces the camera almost square-on, within about 15 degrees, so it reads flat and undistorted; its four edges run parallel to the edges of the photograph, a true rectangle, never a trapezoid or keystone; flat things on a table are shot from nearly straight above. Only the objects named in the shot are in frame. The space shows small honest signs of use; the design surface itself is new and clean. The glowing surface is bright and clean, clearly the brightest thing in the frame, without blowing out; its edges and corners stay crisp. No halation, bloom, haze or glow over it.

Design surface: THE LIGHTBOX FACE IS PLAIN EVENLY LIT WHITE, glowing bright and clean edge to edge, clearly the brightest thing in the frame yet not blown out, with crisp corners meeting its thin black frame; nothing on it and nothing crossing it.

Finish: Shot on 35mm Kodak Portra 800 pushed one stop: natural visible grain in the shadows, true neutral film colour, gentle lens falloff toward the corners, honest exposure that lets the room go dark. Quiet and real, like a page in an exhibition catalogue; never a smooth digital render.

Avoid: a face, chin, lips or profile, logos, letters or brand names anywhere, any image, text or colour on the glowing surface, any object not named in the shot, fog or haze, a clean smooth digital look.
